Q: Some browsers fail to include comments in “Function.prototype.toString” output. Which ones do? What alternatives are there? A:

As of ECMAScript 2019, all implementations of Function.prototype.toString are required to reproduce exactly the original source code that defined the function, if available. See ECMA-262 10th Ed., §19.2.3.5; the [[SourceText]] slot is filled at parse time with the exact source code encountered in the function definition. As such, you should ordinarily expect comments to be preserved. Note that the engine is permitted to withhold source code for user code functions at its discretion. A proposal exists to make it a standard feature that user code may request.

Note that this does not mean that the code will always be a valid stand-alone expression, or that it will be possible to fruitfully parse.

Q: How should people with only one name fill mandatory first name and last name fields? A:

Put your single name in the last name field and drop a period or "N/A" in the first name field. That's the workaround most people use. But if you're the one building the form, just use a single "Full Name" field or make the last name optional. Forcing two separate name fields is a Western design assumption that quietly excludes a large chunk of the world.
